record.paper_title: Open questions regarding the arrow of time
record.context_brief: Initial homogeneity and the Weyl tensor condition
record.original_question: Is the relevant low-entropy condition of the early universe best understood as primordial homogeneity, as Penrose’s vanishing-Weyl-tensor condition on past singularities, or as some closely related condition; and if the Weyl condition cannot be explained by absorptive matter in the way electromagnetic retardation can, must it instead be taken as the law-like ingredient that establishes the causal asymmetry of the universe by excluding future-relevant initial correlations?

evidence.quote: Therefore, the initial homogeneity of the universe becomes a major candidate for the specific low entropy condition that characterizes this universe.
Roger Penrose has formulated this condition in general relativity by postulating a vanishing Weyl tensor on all past singularities.
It may then itself have to establish the causal nature of the universe, that is, it would have to be responsible for the absence of future-relevant initial correlations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In general relativity, the thermodynamic arrow of time is widely associated with a very low-entropy condition imposed on the early universe. Two natural candidates for this condition are:

(a) Primordial homogeneity: the spatial geometry and matter distribution near the initial cosmological singularity are highly homogeneous and isotropic.

(b) The Weyl curvature condition: on every past singularity of spacetime, the Weyl conformal curvature tensor C_{abcd} of the Lorentzian metric vanishes (or is suitably bounded), while the Ricci part of the curvature, governed by the Einstein equations and the matter content, is unconstrained.

By contrast, the well-known explanation of the retardation asymmetry of classical electromagnetism — that physically realized solutions of Maxwell's equations are retarded rather than advanced — can be derived from the assumption that matter is sufficiently absorptive in the future, so that no incoming free radiation field is present.

Address the following:

1. Determine whether the appropriate low-entropy initial condition that selects the observed thermodynamic arrow of time in a general-relativistic universe is best formulated as primordial homogeneity, as the vanishing-Weyl-tensor condition on past singularities, or as some closely related geometric condition; in particular, give a precise mathematical formulation of the chosen condition and prove that it implies a monotonic increase of a suitable coarse-grained entropy along the cosmological time direction.

2. Show whether the Weyl condition can or cannot be derived, in analogy with electromagnetic retardation, from an assumption of "absorption" by the gravitational matter content in the future (e.g., from a future boundary condition on gravitational degrees of freedom together with the Einstein equations).

3. If no such derivation is possible, prove that the condition must instead be imposed as an independent law-like postulate, and that this postulate is what excludes future-relevant initial correlations and thereby establishes the causal asymmetry of the universe.
artifact.status_search_result: The Weyl curvature hypothesis remains an open conjecture in mathematical cosmology. Penrose has continued to advocate it (e.g., in his Conformal Cyclic Cosmology proposal, 2010 onward), but no derivation from a future-absorption-style boundary condition is known, and no rigorous theorem links it to monotone entropy growth in full generality. Partial results exist for specific models (e.g., Tod's work on isotropic singularities and conformal extension across the Big Bang), but the overall question of which initial condition correctly captures the low-entropy past, and whether it must be law-like, is still actively debated.

status_evidence.title: The Weyl Curvature Hypothesis
status_evidence.snippet: The Weyl curvature hypothesis... is unproven... Penrose's hypothesis that the Weyl tensor vanishes at initial singularities remains conjectural.
status_evidence.claim: The hypothesis is still considered an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Tod, Isotropic cosmological singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Partial mathematical results on the Weyl curvature hypothesis are obtained for isotropic singularities, but a general proof or derivation is not given.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results exist; the general status is open.

status_evidence.title: Penrose, Cycles of Time (2010)
status_evidence.snippet: Penrose continues to treat the vanishing-Weyl condition as a law-like postulate rather than a theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Penrose treats the condition as a postulate, consistent with it being unresolved.
